description: This is Israel's national report on food loss and food rescue, published every year since 2015 by Leket Israel, the country's largest food rescue organisation, with the consultancy BDO and in cooperation with the Ministries of Health and Environmental Protection. The tenth edition, covering 2024, estimates the volume and value of food lost along the value chain, from farms through processing and retail to households, the share that could be rescued, and the fall in agricultural production after the war that began in October 2023. Its chapters also cover food insecurity and its health and economic effects, environmental costs of food loss, the benefits of food rescue, an international comparison and policy recommendations. Coverage is national. The full report and a media kit are free and available to download from the report site, in Hebrew; no licence terms are stated. Caveats: figures are modelled estimates built by BDO from national statistics and surveys, not measured flows, and methods are only described in the report. Simulation uses: estimating how much food could be redirected to vulnerable households during a supply crisis, and sizing food bank and redistribution capacity. Related records: the FAO food loss and waste database (data-fao-food-loss-and-waste-database) gives international comparisons, and the WFP global food prices (data-wfp-global-food-prices) track food access.
